title: fix(service-automation)!: a notify node that does not name email fails on a written-out address no user holds
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X8XLfKt3As1Z43DaPWMDwjx)_

Fixes #25758

Clause-②: no (narrowing: a notify node whose channels do not include email, and whose recipients hold an email address no user holds, written out or evaluated by a value expression, bare or as user:ADDRESS, now fails the node at run time instead of reporting success; the seat runs the contract review before the queue)
Metadata-protocol: none

The server half of the card (triage `6396218293`), under the seat's ruling: fail loud, never re-route. The authoring refusal at `os validate` / publish is a `domain:spec` card and is not in this PR.

## What changed

Only the email channel sends to an address itself. The inbox keys its row by the recipient as a user id, and the sms channel texts a user's number or a literal phone number. So on a node that does not name `email`, a written-out address reaches someone only when the messaging resolver maps it to the user who holds it, and the resolver maps only a bare address (it hands the remainder of `user:a@b.c` on as the id with no lookup).

| `notify` node | Written-out recipient | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channels` absent (inbox), `inbox`, or `sms` | address no user holds | `sys_inbox_message` row with the address in `user_id`, which no inbox reads; node **success** | node **fails**, names node, recipient and fix; nothing written |
| same | `user:ADDRESS` (any address) | same junk row, node success | node **fails** |
| same | address a user holds, bare | that user's inbox | unchanged |
| same | no data engine, or the lookup fails | inbox not persisted / junk row, node success | node **fails** (the address could not be checked) |
| `channels` include `email` | any address | sent as written (ruling B) | unchanged |
| any | recipient a value expression computes | per ruling B scope A: junk row, node success | judged like a written-out one, named by its source, never its value (option B, ruled by the maintainer 2026-10-26T08:02Z: commits `d352c68a` + `55f6fc27`) |

- `service-automation` `notify-node.ts`: `resolveRecipients` now also returns `written`, each recipient written out as a string that reads as an address (the same `mailedAddressOf` reading the ruling-B screen uses). New `refuseUndeliverableAddresses` runs only when `channels` do not include `email`: a `user:ADDRESS` entry is refused outright; a bare address is looked up as the resolver looks it up (`sys_user` by `email`, the id projected, system read), and refused when no user holds it. All such recipients of a list are named in one message. The node never adds the `email` channel and never writes the row. The `recipients` help served to the Studio inspector says what a written-out address does.
- Sample message: ``notify: node `alert_exec` names no `channels`, so it delivers to the inbox, the default, and writes out a recipient no user receives: `exec@example.com` (no user holds that address). Only the email channel sends to an address; the others deliver to a user, so nobody would receive it, and nothing was sent. To mail the address as written, add `email` to the node's `channels`. To reach a user, name the user: a user id, an audience selector such as `role:NAME`, or the address that user holds, written bare.``
- `examples/app-showcase` node `alert_exec` (flow `showcase_project_escalation`): `recipients: 'exec@example.com'` on the inbox becomes `recipients: 'role:owner'`. Measured: the showcase's mail goes through `plugin-email`'s default `log` transport, so adding `email` would only log a mail to `example.com`; `role:owner` reaches the organization's owners, and `ensure-default-organization.ts` makes the admin the Default Organization's `owner`, so the "Alert Exec" branch now reaches a real inbox.
- `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: the new test's `findOne` double, written by `check:engine-double-contract --write`.
- Changeset: `@objectstack/service-automation` `patch`, BREAKING banner, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.

## Where the check lives (PM hypothesis, measured)

Channels registered on `main` (`messaging-service-plugin.ts`): `inbox`, `email`, `sms`, no others in the repo. Which take a user id: `inbox` only a user id, and silently keys any value (`inbox-channel.ts:149`, `:205`); `sms` a user id or a literal phone number, and an address there already fails the delivery (`no phone number for recipient`); `email` a user id or an address. The node is the one place that knows both the recipient's provenance (written or computed) and the node's `channels`, so the check is there and covers inbox and sms alike. No channel changes.

## Is it a narrowing (measured against AGENTS.md)

Yes, at run time: a run that used to complete now fails at this node, and a failing node in a `parallel` branch or before later nodes changes what the run does. The parse and `os validate` are unchanged and no key, value or stored shape moves, so `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch`, the precedent of PR #25954 and of the run-time half in `.changeset/25572-*`. The claim's `Clause-②: no` carried no arm; this PR adds `(narrowing: …)`, so the contract review is owed.

## Tests

- New `notify-written-address-channels.integration.test.ts` (10 cases), real `MessagingService` (inline fan-out), real inbox and email channels, data engine recording every row: refusal for inbox default, `inbox`, `sms`, `user:ADDRESS` (unheld and held), a list naming two; controls: an address a user holds reaches that user's inbox, `email` and `inbox`+`email` nodes mail the address as written; no data engine refuses.
- **Red first** (commit `fc0c961b`, before the fix, on `main` `17c5e68b`): 7 failed (every refusal case and the no-engine case, each `expected true to be false` on `run.success`), 3 controls passed.
- Ablation (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, one behaviour: the refusal's early return, `written.length === 0` to `>= 0`; the test imports the node from `src`, no `dist` in the path): 7 failed, 26 passed (the 7 are exactly the refusal cases; the email-field suite stays green). Restore: blob `33f2d3a7` equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Verification

At head `47c6ea05` unless noted, under the verify lock:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation test`: 204 files / 2677 passed; `typecheck` (with `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/example-showcase test`: 39 files / 484 passed; `typecheck`: exit 0 (after building its dependency closure).
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the three changed TypeScript files: exit 0.
- Derived gates and the dogfood battery: in the `os-dev-report` on #25758.

## Acceptance notes

- Out of this PR's rulings: on a node whose `channels` include both `inbox` and `email`, an address no user holds is mailed as written (ruling B), and the inbox delivery for it still writes a row whose `user_id` is the address. Reported, not changed.
- `@objectstack/spec` describe text for `recipients` (`io-node-config.zod.ts`) still says a written-out address goes "to the user who holds it, or else, on the `email` channel, to the address itself" and does not say a node without `email` fails. That is the `domain:spec` half's text.
- Branch is the harness-assigned `claude/project-thread-hdpxcs`; the claim comment `6408881630` is the identity record.
